thread.title: Nintendo: Creating a ‘Poké-Verse’ You Never Need to Leave

title: Nintendo: Creating a ‘Poké-Verse’ You Never Need to Leave
text:
David Marino-Nachison May 30, 2018 11:04 a.m. ET
Nintendo offered a vision of an interlinked videogaming universe on Tuesday, announcing new Pokémon games for the popular Switch console that bridge the gap between that device and mobile phones.
Without getting too deep into Poké-lore, which we don’t understand anyhow, we can boil down that part of the announcement to the part that describes how the games—called “Pokémon: Let’s Go, Pikachu!” and “Pokémon: Let’s Go, Eevee!”—can work with the popular Pokémon Go mobile game, which is availabl e for both the Alphabet -owned (GOOGL) Android and Apple (AAPL) iOS operating systems. (Alphabet and Apple are Barron’s Next 50 stocks.) More About Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50
The upshot: You can catch critters on your phone, then use them on your Switch (which, by the way, is both home console and mobile gaming device ). Nintendo also teased “something special” that will make” the connection between both games even more appealing,” but didn’t offer more detail.
In a stylized trailer available on YouTube , you can get a sense of what they’re describing. Bonus: A brief moment in which a woman pulls out a Nintendo accessory during coffee with a friend; the friend appears to mime a “What ARE you doing?” gesture in response.
As games continue to evolve from what amount to contained one-person experiences to make-believe universes you could theoretically never level, tweaks like this illustrate ways companies will likely seek to keep players connected wherever they might be. As the rise of games like “Fortnite” has shown , “engagement” is increasingly a metric that matters to this industry. Newsletter Sign-up
Augmented reality games like “Go,” now at 800 million downloads , further blur that line—as, perhaps, do related wrinkles in yesterday’s announcement, which included more cooperative play and the aforementioned accessory you can take with you, and use, on the go. Gamers, and investors, should expect more like this.
Meanwhile, the strategy seems like a smart tactic for sustaining Switch sales and perhaps upselling “Go” players. The new games will reportedly cost $60 , while “Go” is free.
